report: Checked all 14 candidate lemmas end to end; every difference is licensed by the ASV's rendering or by the source. The three assimilated articles are read consistently: [הַ] before 'wax' (v5) and 'idols' (v7) unrepresented where the ASV writes no 'the', [הַ] before 'righteous' (v11) aligned to the written 'the' (rule 12).

כֹּל in the multi-level chain אֲדוֹן כָּל־הָאָרֶץ (v5) takes 'of whole' as the rectum of אֲדוֹן (rule 19), matching the 13 corpus units of כֹּל → 'of whole'; v6/v9 'all' are the ordinary reading. Not a split.

Both מִלִּפְנֵי in v5 are read alike: מִן+לְ fused to 'at' headed on מִן (rule 23), פְּנֵי split off to 'the presence' because the ASV spends a word on it (rule 30 subtraction); competing reading (לְ unrepresented) is named in the notes.

Vocative 'ye' is placed by word order in both v7 ('all ye gods') and v12 ('ye righteous'), per rule 36. The two 'He's of v10 differ by construction: the participial clause's 'He' resumes the earlier-written יְהוָה (rule 25, 4 corpus 'jehovah he' units), the finite יַצִּיל takes its own (rule 17).
The one BSB disagreement (v7 לוֹ unrepresented beside 'Worship him') is the documented rule 40 convention for a dative לְ rendered as a bare English object, not an error.
The three repeated notes restate rules 19 and 29 and need no convention. Nothing here generalises beyond the contract; no promotions or amendments.
